quick_skim.title: Shape-Preserving Covariate Adjustment via Empirical Likelihood in Randomized Experiment
quick_skim.abstract: Covariate adjustment improves estimation efficiency in randomized experiments, but standard calibration and augmentation methods, when applied to distribution or survival functions, do not preserve monotonicity---a fundamental property of the estimand. We propose using empirical likelihood with covariate-balancing constraints to construct a covariate-adjusted empirical measure for each treatment arm. Estimators of a broad class of distributional functionals, including cumulative distribution functions, survival functions, quantiles, and restricted mean survival times, are then derived as plug-in functionals of this measure, automatically inheriting proper shape constraints. We establish asymptotic normality with an explicit, guaranteed efficiency gain over unadjusted estimators. The asymptotic distributions are invariant to the randomization scheme, providing a unified inference procedure under simple randomization and all commonly used covariate-adaptive designs satisfying a mild balancing condition. This unified construction, adjusting the empirical measure once and deriving all estimators from it, offers a principled reconciliation of covariate adjustment with shape preservation. Simulations and an application to the SURPASS-4 trial confirm the theoretical gains.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Proposes empirical likelihood covariate adjustment that preserves monotonicity for distribution and survival function estimators in randomized experiments, with asymptotic normality guarantees; directly improves estimation efficiency for survival-type outcomes.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 该研究针对随机实验中协变量调整破坏分布函数或生存函数单调性的问题，提出基于经验似然和协变量平衡约束的调整方法，构造保序的协变量校正经验测度，并证明估计量的渐近正态性。该方法可用于分布函数、生存函数、分位数和受限平均生存时间等泛函，能提升效能。在运动训练影响皮瓣存活的随机试验中，可用于更稳健地估计生存曲线并提高检验效率。
